title: Focus
coreMove: Use a mental model to keep scanning for context when pressure tries to shrink attention to one cue.
sourcePressure: The chapter ties focus to cognitive tunneling, Air France Flight 447, and the power of mental models; it treats narrowed pressure-attention as the danger and prebuilt models as the corrective.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Equating intense attention with good attention.

sourceAnchors.name: Air France Flight 447
sourceAnchors.detail: the source bundle identifies this flight as the focus and mental-models anchor without supporting cockpit detail
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Air France Flight 447 should stand as the high-stakes warning: pressure can make attention feel strong while the field of vision collapses.

sourceAnchors.name: cognitive tunneling
sourceAnchors.detail: the sidecar allows the exact term as the chapter mechanism for pressure-narrowed attention
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Cognitive tunneling is the mind grabbing one bright signal and treating the rest of the scene as background noise.

sourceAnchors.name: mental models
sourceAnchors.detail: the subtitle directly supports mental models as the chapter corrective
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A mental model gives the mind a checklist of what else should still be true before the first cue gets to rule the room.

hook: Person at a meeting realizes the real lesson
The day starts with a dashboard
counterintuition: Productivity is not doing more faster
The problem is not effort but something deeper

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person direct address, retrospective, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

exampleSpecs.domain: a neonatal unit alarm response during a false-code scare
exampleSpecs.audience: a nurse leading a cramped response team
exampleSpecs.stakes: one flashing monitor could hide the real breathing problem
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Megan uses her pre-briefed assessment sequence to check the baby, the line, and the monitor instead of letting the loudest alarm own her attention
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The monitor chirps in a pitch sharp enough to silence the room

exampleSpecs.domain: a cybersecurity incident room during a suspected credential breach
exampleSpecs.audience: an incident commander watching analysts chase the first red alert
exampleSpecs.stakes: the real intrusion path may sit outside the obvious dashboard tile
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: At 11:18 p.m., Julien pauses the alert chase and makes the team map expected attacker steps before touching the next alert
exampleSpecs.firstImage: At 11:18 p.m., a red tile pulses on the security wall

exampleSpecs.domain: a search-and-rescue shoreline sweep after a kayak is found empty
exampleSpecs.audience: a volunteer team lead under pressure from waiting relatives
exampleSpecs.stakes: searchers may over-focus on the kayak and miss wind and tide signals
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Akira asks the team to predict the drift path from wind, tide, and launch point before sending boats toward the visible kayak
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Rain beads on an overturned yellow kayak near the reeds

exampleSpecs.domain: a trial lawyer hearing a surprise witness answer
exampleSpecs.audience: a defense attorney who feels the case turning on one dramatic sentence
exampleSpecs.stakes: overreacting to one answer could miss a contradiction in the record
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Andrew writes the model question at the top of his pad and checks the prior timeline before launching cross-examination
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "I saw the van at nine," the witness says, and the gallery goes still

exampleSpecs.domain: a wilderness first-aid course where a trainee fixates on visible blood
exampleSpecs.audience: an instructor teaching new guides to scan before acting
exampleSpecs.stakes: a fixation on the obvious wound could miss airway or temperature risks
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You watch Anya turn a trainee from the bleeding hand to the full scene by making him narrate the model: airway, heat, bleeding, exit route
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You are kneeling beside pine needles and a red bandana tied too tightly

exampleSpecs.domain: a chess youth final where a player sees only the tempting capture
exampleSpecs.audience: a coach reviewing a position with a talented thirteen-year-old
exampleSpecs.stakes: one flashy move loses the match if the back rank is ignored
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Mikkel covers the attacking piece with a spare score sheet so the player must scan threats, king safety, and tempo
exampleSpecs.firstImage: What would you look at if the capture were not on the board?
mustAvoid: letting the question hook replace the visible action beat

skillTargets: spot cognitive tunneling when someone is intensely focused but under-scanning
choose a mental-model prompt that broadens context
distinguish useful focus from cue fixation

tryThisNowSpec: Before your next pressured choice, say out loud: the cue I see is one signal; the two signals I still need are __ and __.
